samasa.vigraha: तत्त्वानि आसनम् यस्याः सा तत्त्वासना
samasa.vigraha_iast: tattvāni āsanam yasyāḥ sā tattvāsanā
samasa.explanation: The members are tattva 'principle of reality' and āsana 'seat'; the whole is a bahuvrīhi describing Her: 'She whose seat is the tattvas'. The neuter āsana takes the feminine -ā because the compound qualifies the Goddess.

components.meaning: principle of reality, category of existence
components.note: tat 'that' + the abstract suffix -tva: lit. 'that-ness', the true nature of a thing
āsana, with the feminine -ā of the bahuvrīhi

names.meaning: She whose seat is the tattvas, the principles of reality
names.significance: In Śrīvidyā the tattvas, from earth up to Śiva, are the throne on which She is enthroned and worshipped; She rests on all of manifest reality and is not contained by it.

meaning_check.note: The first gloss is kept; the second ('She who abides in tattva') is a different analysis and is given under uncertain.

sandhi.rule: No sound changes here. tat and tvam are simply juxtaposed (t + tv), and the final m of tvam stays m before the vowel of ayī (it becomes anusvāra only before a consonant, Pāṇini 8.3.23 mo 'nusvāraḥ). components.note: neuter nominative singular of the demonstrative pronoun tad

names.meaning: She who is 'That', the supreme reality (brahman)

meaning_check.note: Wording tidied ('meant by' → 'is').

components.note: nominative singular of the second-person pronoun yuṣmad

names.meaning: She who is 'Thou', the self addressed in the teaching 'That thou art'
names.significance: In tat tvam asi the word tvam denotes the individual self (jīva); its identity with tat (425) is the teaching of Advaita. Name 908, tattvamarthasvarūpiṇī, takes up the same pair: She is the meaning of tat and tvam.

meaning_check.note: Reworded: the name is the pronoun 'thou'; the old gloss 'referred to by' added nothing to it.

sandhi.rule: No sound change: the m of tvam stays m before the vowel a of ayī (Pāṇini 8.3.23 makes m anusvāra only before a consonant). Bhāskararāya's division of tattvamayī into tat, tvam and ayī: see name 425.

components.note: an interjection of address; usually written ayi with short i

names.meaning: She who is called upon with the loving cry 'ayī', 'O Mother!'
names.significance: Traditionally ayī is the call of a devotee to the Mother, completing the triad tat, tvam, ayī; some read the three names together as echoing tat tvam asi, 'That thou art'.

names.uncertain: The sense of ayī is not settled. The common interjection of address is ayi with a short i; the long ī here is read either as that particle lengthened or as a feminine form, and the commentarial derivation could not be confirmed here. The rendering follows the usual reading as a call of address.

samasa.type: saptamī-tatpuruṣa (over an inner ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa and a dvigu)
samasa.vigraha: पञ्च कोशाः पञ्चकोशाः; पञ्चकोशानाम् अन्तरम् पञ्चकोशान्तरम्; पञ्चकोशान्तरे स्थिता पञ्चकोशान्तरस्थिता
samasa.vigraha_iast: pañca kośāḥ pañcakośāḥ; pañcakośānām antaram pañcakośāntaram; pañcakośāntare sthitā pañcakośāntarasthitā
samasa.explanation: (1) pañca-kośa 'the five sheaths': a numeral compound, which counts as a dvigu because another member follows (Pāṇini 2.1.51 taddhitārthottarapadasamāhāre ca). (2) …kośa-antara 'the interior of the five sheaths' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa; antara is a noun, 'inside'). (3) The participle sthitā 'abiding' is the head of the whole and takes that interior in the locative. The n of pañcan drops at the end of a compound member; that is morphology, not sandhi.

components.note: appears as pañca- in the compound

names.meaning: She who abides within the five sheaths
names.significance: The five sheaths of the Taittirīya Upaniṣad — of food, breath, mind, understanding and bliss — enclose the Self; She is that innermost Self, hidden within all five.
names.previous_split_issues: kośāntara was glossed as one unit 'within the sheaths'; it is kośa 'sheath' + antara 'interior', fused by savarṇa-dīrgha.

sandhi.rule: the s of nis becomes visarga before the sibilant (s → ru, Pāṇini 8.2.66; ru → visarga before a voiceless sound, 8.3.15), and the visarga is kept instead of becoming s (optional, 8.3.36 vā śari): niḥsīma, also written nissīma

samasa.type: bahuvrīhi (over an inner karmadhāraya and a prādi-compound)
samasa.vigraha: निर्गतः सीम्नः निःसीमः; निःसीमः महिमा यस्याः सा निःसीममहिमा
samasa.vigraha_iast: nirgataḥ sīmnaḥ niḥsīmaḥ; niḥsīmaḥ mahimā yasyāḥ sā niḥsīmamahimā
samasa.explanation: (1) niḥ-sīma 'gone beyond limit, boundless': the prefix nis with the sense of nirgata 'gone out of' compounds with sīman 'boundary' (a prādi-compound; sīman loses its final n). (2) niḥsīma qualifies mahiman 'greatness'. (3) The whole is a bahuvrīhi: 'She whose greatness is boundless'. The an-stem mahiman keeps its form, and its nominative mahimā serves as the feminine.

names.meaning: She whose glory is limitless
names.significance: Her greatness has no boundary in space, time or form; the Upaniṣads speak of brahman as resting in its own greatness.

samasa.vigraha: नित्यम् यौवनम् यस्याः सा नित्ययौवना
samasa.vigraha_iast: nityam yauvanam yasyāḥ sā nityayauvanā
samasa.explanation: nitya 'everlasting' qualifies yauvana 'youth'; the whole is a bahuvrīhi: 'She whose youth is everlasting'. The neuter yauvana takes the feminine -ā.

components.note: yauvana (from yuvan 'young'), with the feminine -ā of the bahuvrīhi

names.meaning: She who is ever youthful
names.significance: Untouched by time, She never ages; compare 470, vayo'vasthāvivarjitā, free from the stages of age.
names.previous_split_issues: yauvanā was glossed 'youthful'; it is the noun yauvana 'youth', made feminine because the compound describes Her.

samasa.vigraha: मदेन शालिनी मदशालिनी
samasa.vigraha_iast: madena śālinī madaśālinī
samasa.explanation: śālinī 'resplendent, abounding' is the head; mada 'exhilaration, rapture' stands to it in the instrumental: 'resplendent with rapture'.

components.note: feminine of śālin, used at the end of compounds

names.meaning: She who is resplendent with rapture (mada)
names.significance: Names 431–433 describe the mada of the Goddess. Traditionally this is the overflowing joy of Her own bliss (ānanda), not ordinary intoxication; in Kaula ritual it is linked with the offering of wine, understood inwardly.

meaning_check.note: 'shining in a state of inebriation' was reworded: śālinī means resplendent with, and mada is rapture.

samasa.type: bahuvrīhi (over an inner tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa and a karmadhāraya)
samasa.vigraha: मदेन घूर्णिते मदघूर्णिते; मदघूर्णिते रक्ते अक्षिणी यस्याः सा मदघूर्णितरक्ताक्षी
samasa.vigraha_iast: madena ghūrṇite madaghūrṇite; madaghūrṇite rakte akṣiṇī yasyāḥ sā madaghūrṇitaraktākṣī
samasa.explanation: (1) mada-ghūrṇita 'rolling with rapture' (tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa). (2) It and rakta 'red' qualify akṣi 'eye'. (3) The whole is a bahuvrīhi: 'She whose eyes are red and rolling with rapture'. At the end of a bahuvrīhi akṣi takes the suffix ṣac (Pāṇini 5.4.113 bahuvrīhau sakthyakṣṇoḥ svāṅgāt ṣac), giving akṣa, and its feminine is akṣī.

components.note: akṣi + the bahuvrīhi suffix ṣac (5.4.113), feminine -ī

names.meaning: She whose eyes are red and rolling with rapture
names.significance: The reddened, rolling eyes are the classical marks of mada; traditionally they show Her absorption in Her own bliss, turned inward.

meaning_check.note: 'inward-looking' is interpretation, not in the name; it is given under significance.

names.previous_split_issues: raktākṣī was glossed as one unit 'red-eyed'; it is rakta 'red' + akṣī 'eye' (akṣi with the bahuvrīhi suffix ṣac).

samasa.type: bahuvrīhi (over an inner tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa and a ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa)
samasa.vigraha: मदेन पाटला मदपाटला; गण्डयोः भूः गण्डभूः; मदपाटला गण्डभूः यस्याः सा मदपाटलगण्डभूः
samasa.vigraha_iast: madena pāṭalā madapāṭalā; gaṇḍayoḥ bhūḥ gaṇḍabhūḥ; madapāṭalā gaṇḍabhūḥ yasyāḥ sā madapāṭalagaṇḍabhūḥ
samasa.explanation: (1) mada-pāṭala 'rosy with rapture' (tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa). (2) gaṇḍa-bhū 'the expanse of the cheeks' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). components.note: nominative of bhū; here 'the surface of the cheeks'

names.meaning: She whose cheeks are rosy with rapture
names.significance: The flush of the cheeks completes the picture of 431–432: the outward signs of Her inner bliss.
names.previous_split_issues: bhūḥ was glossed 'surface/earth' — 'earth' does not apply; gaṇḍa-bhū is the expanse of the cheeks.

samasa.type: bahuvrīhi (over an inner tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa and a ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa)
samasa.vigraha: चन्दनस्य द्रवः चन्दनद्रवः; चन्दनद्रवेण दिग्धानि चन्दनद्रवदिग्धानि; चन्दनद्रवदिग्धानि अङ्गानि यस्याः सा चन्दनद्रवदिग्धाङ्गी
samasa.vigraha_iast: candanasya dravaḥ candanadravaḥ; candanadraveṇa digdhāni candanadravadigdhāni; candanadravadigdhāni aṅgāni yasyāḥ sā candanadravadigdhāṅgī
samasa.explanation: (1) candana-drava 'liquid sandalwood, sandal paste' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (2) …drava-digdha 'anointed with it' (tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa with the past participle). names.meaning: She whose limbs are anointed with sandalwood paste
names.significance: Sandal paste is a cooling unguent and one of the offerings (upacāra) of Her worship; it also links with 458, Her dwelling on the Malaya mountain, home of the sandalwood tree.

samasa.vigraha_iast: cāmpeyasya kusumāni cāmpeyakusumāni; cāmpeyakusumāni priyāṇi yasyāḥ sā cāmpeyakusumapriyā

names.meaning: She who is skillful

samasa.explanation: komala 'tender, soft' qualifies ākāra 'form, figure'; the whole is a bahuvrīhi: 'She whose form is tender'.

names.significance: The terrible and the gentle are both Her forms; here She is gentle, delicate and lovely.

samasa.explanation: (1) kula-kuṇḍa 'the hollow of kula' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa): here kula is the mūlādhāra, and the kuṇḍa the small cavity at its center. (2) The whole is a bahuvrīhi with ālaya 'dwelling' as the final member: 'She whose dwelling is the kulakuṇḍa'.

names.meaning: She who dwells in the kulakuṇḍa, the hollow at the center of the mūlādhāra

meaning_check.note: 'tradition' → 'path' (mārga); Kaula capitalized.

samasa.vigraha: गणानाम् नाथः गणनाथः; कुमारः च गणनाथः च कुमारगणनाथौ; कुमारगणनाथयोः अम्बा कुमारगणनाथाम्बा
samasa.vigraha_iast: gaṇānām nāthaḥ gaṇanāthaḥ; kumāraḥ ca gaṇanāthaḥ ca kumāragaṇanāthau; kumāragaṇanāthayoḥ ambā kumāragaṇanāthāmbā
samasa.explanation: (1) gaṇa-nātha 'lord of the gaṇas', i.e. Gaṇeśa (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (2) kumāra-gaṇanātha 'Kumāra and Gaṇanātha' (itaretara-dvandva). (3) ambā 'mother' is the head, and the pair stands to it in the genitive: 'the mother of both'.

names.meaning: She who is the power of nourishment
names.significance: She nourishes all beings, body and spirit; traditionally the growth of every living thing is Her work.

names.meaning: She who manifests as intelligence

names.meaning: She who is fortitude

report.summary: Checked all 67 names of ślokas 91–100 against text.json, with sandhi at every member junction (and at visible prefix junctions such as ud + jvalā, sam + vṛtā, anu + itā), a layered samāsa analysis with pausa-form vigrahas, and the meanings against that analysis. Bhāskararāya's division tat / tvam / ayī (425–427) is explained (the single word tattvamayī is name 907), and 454 lolākṣīkāmarūpiṇī is analysed as one name. Meanings that were interpretation or belonged to another sense were replaced (448 svastimatī, 454, 466 kṣobhiṇī, 471 siddheśvarī, 481 tvaksthā); the rest were tidied (ITRANS, typos, words not in the name). The yoginī section begins at 475. No problem was found in the Sanskrit text.
